title: Rotate a VCF Automation named credential without stranding in-flight requests
prompt:
Our VCF Automation provider deployment (VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1) needs automated rotation of the secret behind the named credential that our production vCenter registration authenticates with. Security wants that secret changed on a schedule. Operations will not sign off, because the last manual rotation killed requests that were already running against that vCenter.

This repository is where that tooling lives.

Before implementing, research `queryNamedCredentials`, `createNamedCredential`, `getNamedCredential`, `updateNamedCredential`, `deleteNamedCredential`, `testConnection`, `getVirtualCenter`, `updateVirtualCenter`, and `queryAuditTrail` in the official Broadcom VCF Automation Provider Infrastructure xAPIs reference. Confirm their methods, paths, parameters, schemas, status codes, and authentication requirements, and cite the official sources consulted in the final answer. Use only those operations. Because the API documents no grace period, dual-secret window, or credential versioning for an in-place secret update, assume that overwriting a credential immediately invalidates its previous secret.

Implement the two stubbed modules:

- `vcfa_rotate/client.py` — a client for the nine operations named above. An optional body field or query parameter the caller did not set must leave no trace in the request at all — not `null`, not an empty string, list, or object — while an option the caller did set must survive to the wire even when its value is falsy. `None` is the existing signatures' not-supplied sentinel; other explicitly supplied falsy values, including `False`, `0`, `""`, `[]` and `{}`, must survive. Required parameters that have documented defaults still get sent.

- `vcfa_rotate/rotation.py` — implement `rotate_named_credential(...)` so no in-flight vCenter request is stranded. Probe the endpoint before changing anything, resolve the outgoing named credential, read the current vCenter registration, and create a distinct replacement credential instead of overwriting the existing secret. Repoint the vCenter with the new username and password while preserving its required writable configuration and omitting response-only fields. Poll `getVirtualCenter` until it reports `isConnected` true and `listenerState` `CONNECTED`. Then poll `queryAuditTrail` until no event remains `RUNNING`. Only after the vCenter has reconnected and in-flight work has drained may `deleteNamedCredential` retire the outgoing credential. If either wait exceeds `max_polls`, raise `TimeoutError` without deleting the outgoing credential. Return the old and new credential ids, probe result, repoint and retirement task URIs, and drain poll count documented by the stub.

Constraints:

- Python 3.10+ standard library only. No third-party packages.
- Change only `vcfa_rotate/client.py` and `vcfa_rotate/rotation.py`.
- Keep the public signatures already present in the stubs; they are called as documented.

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` must pass.
deliverable: A working stdlib-only implementation of vcfa_rotate/client.py and vcfa_rotate/rotation.py.

verification.notes: All traffic goes to a loopback mock started inside the test process. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. The mock's state transitions are driven by request counts rather than wall-clock time, so the suite gives the same result on every run.
